verses.zh: （大卫在犹大旷野的时候，作了这诗。）　神啊，你是我的　神，我要切切地寻求你，在干旱疲乏无水之地，我渴想你；我的心切慕你。
verses.en: A psalm of David, written when he was in the Judean wilderness.[NOTE:1] O God, you are my God. I long for you.[NOTE:2] My soul thirsts[NOTE:3] for you,my flesh yearns for you,in a dry and parched[NOTE:4] land where there is no water.
notes: Psalm 63. The psalmist expresses his intense desire to be in God’s presence and confidently affirms that God will judge his enemies.
According to the psalm superscription David wrote the psalm while in the “wilderness of Judah.” Perhaps this refers to the period described in 1 Sam 23-24 or to the incident mentioned in 2 Sam 15:23.
Or “I will seek you.”
Or “I thirst.”

verses.zh: 我在圣所中曾如此瞻仰你，为要见你的能力和你的荣耀。
verses.en: Yes,[NOTE:1] in the sanctuary I have seen you,[NOTE:2] and witnessed[NOTE:3] your power and splendor.
notes: Heb “faint” or “weary.” This may picture the land as “faint” or “weary,” or it may allude to the effect this dry desert has on those who are forced to live in it.
The Hebrew particle כֵּן (ken) is used here to stress the following affirmation (see Josh 2:4).

The perfect verbal form is understood here as referring to a past experience which the psalmist desires to be repeated. Another option is to take the perfect as indicating the psalmist’s certitude that he will again stand in God’s presence in the sanctuary. In this case one can translate, “I will see you.”

verses.zh: 因你的慈爱比生命更好，我的嘴唇要颂赞你。
verses.en: Because[NOTE:1] experiencing[NOTE:2] your loyal love is better than life itself,my lips will praise you.
notes: Heb “seeing.” The preposition with the infinitive construct here indicates an accompanying circumstance.

This line is understood as giving the basis for the praise promised in the following line. Another option is to take the Hebrew particle כִּי (ki) as asseverative/emphasizing, “Indeed, your loyal love is better” (cf. NEB, which leaves the particle untranslated).

verses.zh: 我还活的时候要这样称颂你；我要奉你的名举手。
verses.en: For this reason[NOTE:1] I will praise you while I live;in your name I will lift up my hands.[NOTE:2]
notes: The word “experiencing” is supplied in the translation for clarification. The psalmist does not speak here of divine loyal love in some abstract sense, but of loyal love revealed and experienced.
Or perhaps “then.”

verses.zh: 我在床上记念你，在夜更的时候思想你；我的心就像饱足了骨髓肥油，我也要以欢乐的嘴唇赞美你。
verses.en: As with choice meat[NOTE:1] you satisfy my soul.[NOTE:2] My mouth joyfully praises you,[NOTE:3]
notes: I will lift up my hands. Lifting up one’s hands toward God was a gesture of prayer (see Ps 28:2; Lam 2:19) or respect (Ps 119:48).
Heb “like fat and fatness.”
Or “me.”

verses.en: whenever[NOTE:1] I remember you on my bed,and think about you during the nighttime hours.
notes: Heb “and [with] lips of joy my mouth praises.”

verses.zh: 因为你曾帮助我，我就在你翅膀的荫下欢呼。
verses.en: For you are my deliverer;[NOTE:1] under your wings[NOTE:2] I rejoice.
notes: The Hebrew term אִם (ʾim) is used here in the sense of “when; whenever,” as in Ps 78:34.
Or “[source of] help.”

verses.zh: 我心紧紧地跟随你；你的右手扶持我。
verses.en: My soul[NOTE:1] pursues you;[NOTE:2] your right hand upholds me.
notes: Heb “in the shadow of your wings.”
Or “I.” The Hebrew term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) with a pronominal suffix is often equivalent to a pronoun, especially in poetry (see BDB 660 s.v. נֶפֶשׁ 4.a).

verses.zh: 但那些寻索要灭我命的人必往地底下去；
verses.en: Enemies seek to destroy my life,[NOTE:1] but they will descend into the depths of the earth.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “clings after.” The expression means “to pursue with determination” (see Judg 20:45; 1 Sam 14:22; 1 Chr 10:2; Jer 42:16).
Heb “but they for destruction seek my life.” The pronoun “they” must refer here to the psalmist’s enemies, referred to at this point for the first time in the psalm.

verses.zh: 他们必被刀剑所杀，被野狗所吃。
verses.en: Each one will be handed over to the sword;[NOTE:1] their corpses will be eaten by jackals.[NOTE:2]
notes: The depths of the earth refers here to the underworld dwelling place of the dead (see Ezek 26:20; 31:14, 16, 18; 32:18, 24). See L. I. J. Stadelmann, The Hebrew Conception of the World, 167.

Heb “they will deliver him over to the sword.” The third masculine plural subject must be indefinite (see GKC 460 §144.f) and the singular pronominal suffix either representative or distributive (emphasizing that each one will be so treated). Active verbs with indefinite subjects may be translated as passives with the object (in the Hebrew text) as subject (in the translation).

verses.zh: 但是王必因　神欢喜。凡指着他发誓的必要夸口，因为说谎之人的口必被塞住。
verses.en: But the king[NOTE:1] will rejoice in God;everyone who takes oaths in his name[NOTE:2] will boast,for the mouths of those who speak lies will be shut up.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “they will be [the] portion of jackals”; traditionally, “of foxes.”
The psalmist probably refers to himself in the third person here.
Heb “who swears [an oath] by him.”
